sample_unit: clinical vignettes (HealthBench Hard), 5 random seeds, 2000 observations

links.outcome: Clinical response quality, hedging (humility) and context-seeking with vs without BODHI uncertainty framework
links.effect: Overall quality +16.6 pp (GPT-4.1-mini, d=11.56) and +2.2 pp (GPT-4o-mini, d=1.56); hedging d=5.80 for GPT-4.1-mini; context seeking d=16.38 and 19.54.
links.quote: BODHI improved overall clinical response quality (GPT-4.1-mini: +16.6 pp, p<0.0001, Cohen's d=11.56; GPT-4o-mini: +2.2 pp, p<0.0001, Cohen's d=1.56) and achieved very large effect sizes on curiosity (context seeking rate: Cohen's d=16.38 and 19.54) and humility (hedging: d=5.80 for GPT-4.1-mini) metrics.

unlisted_practices: Virtue-based stance rules and epistemic uncertainty decomposition to make LLMs seek clarifying information (curiosity) and hedge appropriately

screen.practice: prompt guardrails with uncertainty decomposition and virtue-based stance rules
screen.reason: Evaluates an engineering framework / guardrail mechanism (BODHI) that applies structured uncertainty decomposition and virtue-aligned response rules to LLMs, testing outcomes on clinical vignettes.

primary.practice: virtue-based stance rules and uncertainty decomposition guardrails
